comment: The README writes the decision as !(v1<Cmp1 XOR v2<Cmp2) XOR v3<Cmp3 and describes the menu as inverting a 'less than' test; the installed code compares with 'at or above' and takes !(b1 XOR b2) XOR b3 from those results, which is the same shape with the sense of each test turned around. The README does not mention the Mod/SR/Seq switch, the PosO knob or the SR output, which are all in this build. The In jack carries whatever signal you patch, so it has no family. The CV output carries one channel. SEQMod.cpp:183 writes sixteen channels of it in a loop but the module never calls setChannels() on it, so only the first reaches a cable.
